The meal that comes second in the day, after breakfast, is lunch.

Regarding the thematic structure in the provided text, the author’s motive appears to be an exploration of the parallel between natural decay and human emotional states. By using the wilting sunflower as a botanical metaphor for the protagonist’s sadness and isolation, the author links the inevitable cycle of life and decay in nature to the fragility of human connection. This structure serves to urge readers to reflect on how neglect—whether directed at a plant or a relationship—leads to deterioration, thereby emphasizing the importance of care and connection in both the natural and social worlds.
